feature1.prompt: Unused-import false positive for a module used in a type comment presents an issue where a module imported only for type annotation purposes is incorrectly flagged as unused. In the reproduced scenario, code imports a module (for example, 'abc') and later refers to its members in type comments; however, a warning is emitted even though the module is being used. The expected behavior is that when a module is referenced in a type comment, no unused-import warning (W0611) should be produced. This feature focuses on correcting the type comment handling logic so that attribute references within type annotations are properly recognized.
feature1.hint_texts: This feature involves modifying the type annotation processing in the variable checker. Developers should update the function responsible for storing type annotation nodes so that it examines whether the annotation is an attribute. When an attribute is detected, its underlying expression should be recorded appropriately to signify its usage. This change will prevent the unused-import warning from being triggered when the module is only used in type comments.
feature1.entrypoint: File: pylint/checkers/variables.py, Function: _store_type_annotation_node. Investigate the logic around handling different types of AST nodes, particularly after line 1826, and add a check for type_annotation being an instance of astroid.Attribute.

This feature is part of the overall fix and supports environment-sensitive configuration to ensure robustness of the solution.
